summary: Registered the follow-up that closes the one half of the read-index behaviour still resting on source reading: a child question @readindex_leadership_loss under the read-index question, with the scenario spelled out — elect a leader while withholding the append acknowledgement, queue a read request, let the leader be demoted by its own quorum check and another node take leadership at a higher term, confirm no read state appears for the queued request while that node is a follower, then let it lead again and commit to see whether the stale request is released at all and with which index. The hypothesis is the source reading (nothing clears the queue on a term change and the release helper is only reachable from a leader commit path, so such a request is answered only if that node leads again and commits, otherwise never — an outcome the interface documentation permits), and the discriminator names what would refute it: a read state appearing while the node is a follower, or a release with an index older than the one recorded at acceptance, which would turn the account into a safety finding. The harness can now support this because the delivery helper writes Ready entries to storage, so commits in a term actually happen. Validation passed with no execution requested; the experiment for this question is the next step.
